meal.name: Ekpang Nkukwo
description: An Efik/Ibibio pottage of small leaf-wrapped portions of grated hairy cocoyam and water yam.
This published pumpkin-leaf wrapper variant uses beef, dried fish, shelled periwinkles, palm oil and scent leaf.
reasons: Grating and wrapping distinguish Ekpang from ordinary root chunks.
The small parcels set before gentle stirring.
Palm oil and seafood season the thick pottage.

ingredients.name: tender ugu or fluted-pumpkin leaves for wrappers
ingredients.quantity: about 200 g; enough small leaves for all parcels

ingredients.name: water for parcels
ingredients.quantity: 800 ml initially; enough to reach parcels

instructions: Prepare cleaned beef, chopped onion and pepper; debone fish and inspect periwinkles. Wash wrappers and scent leaf. Grate the peeled cocoyam and water yam finely and mix. Wear kitchen gloves if the raw tuber irritates your hands; do not taste it raw.
Heat beef with half the onion, salt and its water for 5 minutes, then simmer covered for an estimated 45 minutes until tender. Add fish for 10 minutes. Reserve meat and liquid.

Oil a heavy pot with 1 tablespoon of the measured palm oil. Place about 1 teaspoon of grated mixture on each small pumpkin leaf, fold around it and arrange the parcels in layers. Allow about 35 minutes for wrapping.

Add beef, fish, periwinkles, crayfish, pepper, remaining onion and the reserved liquid. Boil the parcel water separately for 5 minutes and pour in enough to reach the parcels. Cook gently, covered, for about 35 minutes without stirring; top up with hot water if drying.

Add the remaining palm oil and sliced scent leaf. Cook 10 minutes more until a center parcel is fully cooked and no raw tuber remains; periwinkles must reach at least 63 C. Stand off heat for 5 minutes, then fold gently and serve.
